the transcriptional regulation of RhoA gene, a key regulator in cell migration and metastasis.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Skp2, a known oncogene, can regulate transcription of a key oncogene, RhoA, by interacting with Myc, Miz1 and p30, and that the transcriptional regulation of RhoA by the Skp2-Myc complex is critical for cell motility, invasion and metastasis.

we have identified a transcriptional complex critical in the expression of RhoA gene and cancer metastasis, and that the complex is comprised of the transcription factors Myc and Miz1, and the E3-ligases Skp2 and p300.
Skp2 and Miz1 cooperate with p300 and Myc to orchestrate RhoA expression and breast cancer metastatic progression.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Skp2-Miz1-p300 transcriptional complex plays a crucial role in regulating RhoA gene transcription and that Skp2-Myc-Miz1-p30 complex may be a potential therapeutic target for breast cancer metastasis.
the Myc–p300–Miz1 transcriptional complex is critical for Rho A transcription.
Skp2 can function as a transcription factor independent of its E3 ligase function, which has important implications for cancer biology.
